messages:
support-ops: customer-42 reports a sharp burst of 504s and 5xxs hitting the hosted inference API around 15:02 UTC. they say checkout flow timed out. attaching a sample request id: req_0a3f1c80. escalating to SRE :rotating_light:

eli-sre: on it. are there any logs / req ids? which model and region?

support-ops: req_0a3f1c80 + req_0a3f2f91. region us-west-2, model: rdl/llama-compact-13b-q4. spike shows ~110-140 rps for ~45s. gateway logs show repeated 504s and a few 502/503s.

deploy-bot: Alert: gateway-frontend/us-west-2 — 504 spike (3.1% of traffic) at 2025-09-12T15:02:07Z

jamal-sre: looking at cluster events and autoscaler. preliminary: KEDA ScaledObject didn't scale because activationThreshold appears too high for per-tenant distribution, and pods that did come up took ~50s to become ready (model init). combined effect -> request queueing then gateway timeouts.

maria-runtime: model cold-start for that variant is ~60s to load weights + 20s to warm key/value cache in our measurements. default gateway timeout is 30s, so anything that waits for a new pod to finish will 504.

jamal-sre: here's relevant ScaledObject snippet and events:
```
kubectl get scaledobject inference-pool-llama -o yaml
metrics:
  - type: external
    external:
      metricName: redis-queue-length
      threshold: 200
minReplicaCount: 0
pollingInterval: 30
cooldownPeriod: 300
```
Events: Activation not triggered, scale to 0 -> 1 delayed 30s, subsequent readiness probe failed until model loaded.

eli-sre: that threshold looks wrong for how we bucket traffic per-tenant. during bursts each tenant had ~80 qps so queue-length never reached 200. also pollingInterval 30s + cooldown 300s means slow reaction.

maria-runtime: additionally readiness probe is simple TCP check. the container is 'ready' before model load completes, so the request path still blocks on model init and times out. we should change readiness to an application-level check (model.kv.ready) and add a priming step.

eli-sre: immediate mitigation plan (short-lived):
- set minReplicaCount=1 for inference-pool-llama for the affected customer tier
- lower external.metric threshold to 20 and pollingInterval to 5s for burst-prone pools
- extend gateway timeout to 75s for customer-42 requests (to avoid UX hit while we stabilize)
- enable a fast-fallback route to a smaller model for latency-sensitive endpoints

commands I'll run now:
```
kubectl patch scaledobject inference-pool-llama --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":1}}'
kubectl apply -f keda-tuning/inference-pool-llama-patch.yaml
```

jamal-sre: running patch. also adding an annotation to skip cooldown for next 5m.

ci-bot: patch deployed to staging, rollout to prod queued (change id: CHG-5421).

maria-runtime: follow-ups we should track: optimize model load path (stream weights + lazy init), add KV prewarm in container entrypoint, change readiness probe to check model readiness endpoint, and add a priming job that preloads a small cache when new replicas start.

eli-sre: customer comms: support-ops — recommend offering a partial credit and let them know we applied temporary config changes; promise a follow-up with timeline for long-term fix.

support-ops: will notify customer-42 with interim workaround and ETA. priority = high.

jamal-sre: root cause summary for postmortem: autoscaling misconfiguration (threshold + pollingInterval + cooldown) combined with long model cold-start and inadequate readiness detection -> scale-up lag and gateway timeouts. action items assigned: jamal-sre -> autoscale config defaults and emergency playbook; maria-runtime -> reduce cold-start & implement readiness; eli-sre -> implement fallback routing and temporary TTL-based longer timeouts for affected customers; support-ops -> customer comms + credits.

eli-sre: adding monitoring follow-up: per-tenant qps histogram, time-to-ready metric on pods (container start -> model.ready), and KEDA activation latency metric.

support-ops: new ticket INC-3289 created with notes and timeline. I'll bump priority and include sample logs/req ids. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
